chapter: New York, the Kentucky Club and the high-hat
title: Drum kit before 1930 and the first sock cymbals
summary: Greer describes his early drum set and the wooden foot-clappers that preceded the high-hat.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Jimmy Crawford told me that when he went into the Cotton Club when Lunceford was there, that was the first thing, you cannot work in here if you ain't got that stuff, so he had to go out there and get ahold of stuff.

Now, at that time, let's just fill in, before we go on because now we're up to the Cotton Club, but what kind of equipment had you used before then? I got photographs of you -- hold it a moment. (Recording interruption) Bass drum, snare drum, high hat, two tom toms, two 16-inch tom toms on the floor and two medium sized, up top on the bass drum.
That's what I used then. That's all I used now when I played little quick gigs.
1930, you were using the smaller set then, because that photograph we just looked at you had a big bass drum, one cymbal.
Oh, yeah, this was long before we ever come to New York. This was cabarets, Thomas' Cafe/ in Washington. That's all the drums I used, just a boogershoot, man.
: So you didn't use any sock cymbal then.
